Trail 405, track T1. Branch from origin/main as `feat/jsx-evidence-in-extractor`. Read first: /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md and the trail's plan: the owner wants relevance of props decided from evidence, not name lists. This track only COLLECTS evidence in the extractor; it must not change any output. Cap: 80 tool calls; stop and report what you have verified. Do NOT push: commit locally, report the SHA; I review the diff first.
Collect, per component (the mapping the extractor already builds: crates/core/src/extractor, see visit.rs, component.rs, written.rs, uses.rs, and the collected types in crates/core/src/types/collected.rs), purely syntactically from the oxc AST of the component function body (not nested components; handle function declarations, arrow functions, forwardRef/memo/factory-wrapped functions the extractor already unwraps):
 (a) `reads`: the prop names the function reads: names destructured from the first parameter pattern (renamed, defaulted, nested), the rest binding's name if any, and `props.x` / `props['x']` member reads of the first parameter identifier anywhere in the body.
 (b) `elements`: for every JSX element in the body: the tag as a kind (intrinsic: lowercase-first or namespaced per JSX rules; identifier; member path like `chakra.button`) with the identifier text, and its attributes IN SOURCE ORDER: for a named attribute: its name and whether the value is exactly one of the component's own props (the destructured name, `props.x`, or a rest member), for a spread attribute: what is spread (the props identifier, the rest binding, or another expression, recorded as such). Also record whether a `{...x}` spread occurs before or after each named attribute (order is the data; do not interpret it here).
 (c) `handedOn`: whether the first parameter (or rest) is passed whole as a call argument (`useX(props)`) or a JSX spread of the whole props object: a flag, no interpretation.
Store it in the extractor's collected output (SourceData) so it flows to the resolver later, but do NOT emit it in the CLI JSON, napi output or any public type; it is an internal field. Because SourceData is cached, bump CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION and update the golden snapshot test the repo has for it (crates/core/src/cache/golden.rs and its .snap): read how and why first.
Rules: no heuristics from names (DOM vs component is the JSX rule, not a list); no decisions here about relevance, forwarding or subtraction: collect facts only. Tests that fail on origin/main (evidence absent): fixtures for plain destructuring with rename/default/rest, `props.x` reads, a DOM spread, a component spread, attribute before vs after a spread, `{...props}`, `useX(props)`, forwardRef and memo wrapped functions, a component with two return branches, a nested inline component (its elements must not leak into the parent), a conditional/ternary JSX, `React.createElement` (record nothing; say so). Gates, judged by exit code: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, nextest of crates/core, and an identity diff (JSON parsed, stats dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` with AND without `--no-checker` against a build of origin/main on checker-default/chakra-only/src and gate-large/src (both under /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures) and on the corpora shadcn-ui, react-spectrum, mantine, ant-design (/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/corpora; src dirs in scripts/corpora.py): output must be identical. Cost check: the structural pass must not slow down by more than 3% (compare `--no-checker` on gate-large with `perf stat`-style instruction counts or user+sys time over 7 interleaved runs, report `uptime` load). Memory: report the cache size change. Do NOT run the unfixed 0.11.0 binary on the Chakra corpus. Use your own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/ and rust 1.99.1 first on PATH. Read your own diff for guesses before committing. PR body to /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/feat-jsx-evidence-in-extractor.md (`## What`, `## Evidence`, `## Not verified`, session URL line from your system reminder); changeset only if the repo convention requires one for an internal change (it does not change output). Final message at most 120 words.

semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    status=0
    for crate in caliper-docgen-core caliper-docgen-semantic; do
        if cargo semver-checks check-release -p "$crate"; then
            continue
        fi
        if grep -qsE "^cargo/$crate: (minor|major)$" .changeset/*.md; then
            echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for $crate"
            continue
        fi
        echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/$crate" >&2
        status=1
    done
    exit "$status"

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
